files.purpose: Owns the app window's custom chrome on macOS: turns the SwiftUI hosting NSWindow into a transparent-titlebar, clear, full-size-content-view window; repositions and pins AppKit's three traffic-light buttons with Auto Layout depending on whether the sidebar is showing; stretches the private titlebar container view down so those relocated buttons still receive clicks; and holds the sidebar's width/visibility model (SidebarLayout) plus the AppKit drag strip (SidebarResizeHandle / SidebarResizeHandleView) that resizes and collapses the sidebar.

side_effects: Mutates the host NSWindow in configure: styleMask.insert(.fullSizeContentView), titlebarAppearsTransparent = true, titleVisibility = .hidden, titlebarSeparatorStyle = .none, isOpaque = false, backgroundColor = .clear, hasShadow = true, isMovableByWindowBackground = false, invalidateShadow(), autorecalculatesKeyViewLoop = true

Reaches into AppKit's private titlebar hierarchy: standardWindowButton(.closeButton)?.superview is the button bar and ?.superview?.superview is the titlebar container, whose frame is assigned directly to stretch the titlebar

Sets button.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false and activates four constraints per traffic-light button the first time; afterwards only updates constraint.constant by matching constraint.identifier
Sets button.isHidden = false for all three traffic lights on every placement

Registers and removes NotificationCenter observers for NSWindow.didEndLiveResizeNotification (on the window) and NSView.frameDidChangeNotification (on the titlebar container); sets container.postsFrameChangedNotifications = true; removes all observers in deinit
Spawns a @MainActor Task from titlebarFrameDidChange so the fit runs after AppKit's current layout pass
Spawns a cancellable @MainActor Task in beginSlide that sleeps slideRun milliseconds then clears isSliding and slideDelta
Writes UserDefaults in persist(): Double(restingWidth) under "sidebarWidth" and startsOpen under "sidebarStartsOpen"; called from the startsOpen didSet, endDrag() and toggle()
Reads the same two UserDefaults keys in init()
Runs NSAnimationContext animation groups and CATransaction animations, and calls titlebar.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()
Registers a .columnResize cursor rect and rebuilds an NSTrackingArea; invalidates cursor rects when isActive flips
No file writes, no process launches, no network calls, no keychain access
platform_assumptions: macOS / AppKit only: two NSViewRepresentable bridges from SwiftUI into NSView

Depends on AppKit's traffic lights being real NSViews reachable through NSWindow.standardWindowButton and on their undocumented superview chain (button bar inside a titlebar container inside the theme frame)
Assumes AppKit re-tiles the titlebar container back to its own height on window resize and announces it through frameDidChangeNotification, which is what puts the fit back on
Handles both flipped and unflipped theme-frame coordinate systems in fitTitlebar via themeFrame.isFlipped
Uses the macOS window style mask .fullSizeContentView, titlebarSeparatorStyle .none and titlebarAppearsTransparent
Relies on NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion (the macOS Reduce Motion setting) for both animation durations and slideRun
Uses Swift Observation (@Observable, @ObservationIgnored), @MainActor isolation and Swift concurrency Task/Task.sleep(for:)

Comment records a macOS 26 specific hang: with autorecalculatesKeyViewLoop off, SwiftUI rebuilt the key view loop synchronously on every focusable or AppKit view shape change, and that walk never ended inside the composer's follow-up queue tab, freezing the main thread until force quit (the Sept 15 2026 freezes, FocusBridge.updateDefaultKeyViewLoop at the top of every sample); Full Keyboard Access is named as what makes Tab move between controls at all
Uses NSCursor.columnResize, acceptsFirstMouse(for:) for first-click tracking, and mouseDownCanMoveWindow = false to defeat AppKit's titlebar window dragging
effectiveAppearance.performAsCurrentDrawingAppearance to resolve NSColor.labelColor into a CGColor, plus viewDidChangeEffectiveAppearance for light/dark switches
window.mouseLocationOutsideOfEventStream for polling the real cursor position
persisted_fields: "sidebarWidth": Double in UserDefaults, read as defaults.object(forKey:) as? Double mapped to CGFloat; default SidebarLayout.defaultWidth = 268; clamped on read to min 210 and max 440; written as Double(restingWidth)

"sidebarStartsOpen": Bool in UserDefaults, read as defaults.object(forKey:) as? Bool; default false, so the sidebar starts collapsed; drives startsOpen, the initial isVisible and the initial holdsTrafficLights
Store used for both: CaptureRun.defaults ?? UserDefaults.standard
ui_elements: Native macOS traffic lights (close, miniaturize, zoom), repositioned by constraints; each pinned 14x14 (Chrome.trafficLightDiameter) with x = leading + CGFloat(index) * Chrome.trafficLightPitch for index 0, 1, 2 in the order [.closeButton, .miniaturizeButton, .zoomButton]
Sidebar-visible placement: leading = Chrome.trafficLightLeading (18), top = Chrome.trafficLightTop (16)

Sidebar-hidden placement: leading = Chrome.sheetInset + Chrome.chromeHorizontalPadding (0 + 14 = 14), top = collapsedTrafficLightTop = Chrome.sheetInset + Chrome.chromeTopPadding + (Chrome.capsuleHeight - Chrome.trafficLightDiameter) / 2, i.e. centred on the chat chrome capsule row

titlebarHeight = Chrome.sheetInset + Chrome.chromeTopPadding + Chrome.capsuleHeight: the titlebar is stretched down to the bottom of the chrome row so relocated buttons still take clicks and hovers; the comment notes the side effect that the row's gaps drag the window like a titlebar while the controls on it do not
Constraint identifiers used to find and update constants later: "droppycode.trafficLight.leading" and "droppycode.trafficLight.top"

Traffic-light move animation: NSAnimationContext duration 0.32 normally, 0.18 with Reduce Motion; CAMediaTimingFunction(name: .easeOut); allowsImplicitAnimation = true; skipped entirely (plain layoutSubtreeIfNeeded) when animated is false or window.inLiveResize
Sidebar metrics: minimumWidth 210, maximumWidth 440, collapseThreshold 110, defaultWidth 268
SidebarLayout.slideRun = 420 ms normally, 220 ms with Reduce Motion
Grip bar: width 2.5, cornerRadius width / 2 = 1.25, rest height 10, shown height 22, opacity 0.6 when shown otherwise 0, frame x = (bounds.width - 2.5) / 2 and y = (bounds.height - height) / 2

Glow panel: cornerRadius 4, opacity 0.05 on hover and 0.10 while dragging, 0 otherwise; frame x = bounds.minX + 0.5, y = Grip.verticalInset = Chrome.trafficLightTop + Chrome.trafficLightDiameter = 16 + 14 = 30, width = max(0, bounds.width - 1), height = max(0, bounds.height - 30)
Grip and glow animation: CATransaction duration 0.18 with easeOut, or setDisableActions(true) when not animated
Both grip and glow are NSColor.labelColor resolved in the view's effective appearance, so they follow light and dark
Cursor over the active strip: NSCursor.columnResize
No user-visible text strings are defined in this file
feature_notes: The window is chromeless by composition: transparent titlebar, hidden title, clear non-opaque background, no titlebar separator (the comment says a focused window's separator would cut through the rounded corner), shadow kept on, and background dragging disabled
configure(_:) is idempotent through a weak NSHashTable because viewDidMoveToWindow fires on every reorder, so the setup pays once per window

autorecalculatesKeyViewLoop = true is a deliberate fix, not a default: with it on, SwiftUI only marks the loop dirty and keeps its focus items by the finite group-based route, and nothing is rebuilt during layout

Traffic lights are never animated mid-live-resize because a fresh animation group every frame made them lag behind the window; they follow unanimated and a final unanimated placement plus fitTitlebar runs on NSWindow.didEndLiveResizeNotification
Traffic lights are also placed unanimated while the sidebar edge is being dragged (sidebarDragging = true), so they track the drag exactly
fitTitlebar only ever grows the container (guard fitted.height < titlebarHeight) and keeps the top edge fixed; in an unflipped theme frame it sets origin.y = maxY - titlebarHeight

titlebarFrameDidChange coalesces work: it queues nothing if the container already has at least titlebarHeight or a fit is already pending, and the queued fit is a frame assignment only, never a synchronous layout or draw
WindowChromeProbeView.hitTest returns nil, so the probe view never intercepts mouse events
The first placement on entering a window is unanimated (animated: false)

Sidebar collapse by drag: releasing below collapseThreshold 110 hides the sidebar with Chrome.panelSlide and snaps width back to restingWidth; otherwise the width settles at max(minimumWidth, width), becomes the new restingWidth and springs there with Chrome.panelSlide. Either way persist() runs and isDragging clears

beginDrag() from a hidden sidebar sets width = 0 and isVisible = true inside a Transaction with disablesAnimations = true, so the sidebar can be dragged out from the edge with no jump; from a visible sidebar it just anchors at the current width
drag(by:) clamps to 0...maximumWidth, so the lower bound during a drag is 0 rather than minimumWidth and the edge can be pulled past the collapse point

toggle() opens from restingWidth and starts a slide whose slideDelta is -restingWidth when opening and +width when closing; the chat pane uses slideDelta and isSliding to treat the slide as one pane reshape with a single layout width rather than a spring
isSliding is cleared by a cancellable task after slideRun ms (420, or 220 with Reduce Motion), the point at which Chrome.panelSlide's spring is judged visually settled

holdsTrafficLights flips from the width actually laid out each frame via noteLaidOutWidth, not from the target state, so the buttons move into the sidebar's corner only once it is genuinely wide enough and the chrome closes up at the same moment; unchanged widths write no state, and lastLaidOutWidth starts at -1 so the first report always lands
renderedWidth is width when visible and 0 when hidden

The resize strip refreshes hover from the real cursor position (window.mouseLocationOutsideOfEventStream converted into view space) in layout(), viewDidMoveToWindow() and on mouseUp, because a toggle or a spring-back can carry the strip out from under a resting cursor and AppKit only reports enter and exit for mouse movement; layout() animates the grip only when that recheck actually changed isHovering
The strip refuses window dragging (mouseDownCanMoveWindow = false) even though its top runs through the stretched titlebar, and accepts first mouse so an inactive window can be resized in one click
When isActive is false the strip has no cursor rect, no hover and hitTest returns nil, so it is fully inert; showsGrip is isActive && (isHovering || isDragging)
The tracking area is rebuilt in updateTrackingAreas with rect .zero and options [.mouseEnteredAndExited, .activeAlways, .inVisibleRect]
Drag deltas are reported as event.locationInWindow.x - pressOriginX, with the final delta sent once more on mouseUp before onEnd, and the grip animates on both mouseDown and mouseUp

All code in this file is shipped: there are no compile conditions, debug flags, or unreachable branches; the only non-executing references are the two names that appear solely in comments (NoWindowDragArea, FocusBridge.updateDefaultKeyViewLoop)
unresolved_questions: Chrome.capsuleHeight is computed elsewhere (DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/Chrome.swift, not in this bundle) as capsuleContentHeight + capsuleVerticalPadding * 2, so the numeric values of titlebarHeight and collapsedTrafficLightTop cannot be stated as literals from this file alone
Chrome.trafficLightSpacing, used by trafficLightPitch and trafficLightsWidth, is also defined outside this bundle, so the exact button pitch and trafficLightsFitWidth stay symbolic here
Chrome.panelSlide's exact spring parameters are defined elsewhere; this file only asserts the spring is visually settled by 420 ms, or 220 ms with Reduce Motion
CaptureRun.defaults is defined outside this bundle, so which UserDefaults suite the two sidebar keys land in, and whether it is nil outside capture runs, cannot be determined here
Who constructs WindowChromeConfigurator and SidebarResizeHandle, and what drives SidebarResizeHandle.isActive and the calls to noteLaidOutWidth, is outside this file
NoWindowDragArea is named only in a comment; its implementation and the guarantee that every chrome control carries one cannot be verified from this file
